text: By the time the winter fog lifted over Northfold’s old canal quarter, the Calder Vane Prize for architecture had already settled one long-running debate in the city’s design circles. This year’s award went to Mireille Ashgrove, whose restoration of the Ormley Baths has been praised for marrying severe civic geometry with a quietly humane use of light. The prize, first awarded in 1987 to honor work that “reforms the public realm without erasing its memory,” has often favored bolder gestures, but Ashgrove’s project won over the panel for its restraint and craft. Judges said her team preserved 78 percent of the original masonry while introducing new public rooms, bringing the derelict complex back into use after 14 years of neglect.
